provenance.definitionOrigin: M6B extends the M6A multi-scene fresh-run manifest with a Q68 fixed-pulley composition; M5/M6A original manifests remain unchanged.
provenance.note: All four scenes must be freshly compiled and all source/result mappings pinned to the native recordings.

notes: BodyBox center of mass equals cartPosition for this authored model; it must not be assumed for arbitrary bodies.
The ideal guide can exert a force and a couple. View the torque quantity as well when interpreting the cart free body.
Guide force and guide couple act on the cart at cartGuide.frame_b; the hinge force acts at pivotPosition.
The rod is massless and the bob is a PointMass. The displayed sphere has no additional rotational inertia.

overlays.signConvention: Force exerted by the wall spring on the cart; the native spring connector force is INTO the spring, so the model alias negates it.

overlays.label: Hinge → cart
overlays.signConvention: Force exerted by the pendulum through the hinge on the cart; opposite to the force INTO hinge.frame_a.

overlays.label: Guide → cart
overlays.signConvention: Bilateral guide reaction on the cart. This is a constraint reaction, not a unilateral contact normal.

overlays.label: Weight → cart

notes: Each BodyBox frame_a coincides with its center of mass in this specific model.
The springs are massless; negate their connector flow forces to obtain force ON each attached block.
R.T maps world vectors into the connector frame; transpose(R.T) maps connector force into the world frame.
FreeMotion joints provide no support force. The drawn upper marker is disconnected scenery.
This recorded run is symmetric and nonrotating, but the metadata export uses each saved full 3 by 3 rotation matrix instead of assuming identity.

notes: Two separate fixed Revolute joints, two massless FixedTranslation rods, two PointMass bobs and one spring are composed entirely from standard Modelica MultiBody components.
The spring joins the two bob frames directly. It exerts equal and opposite forces. Neither angle is prescribed.
The rod and spring arrows are native Modelica connector forces resolved into world axes and explicitly negated to denote forces ON each bob.
Weight overlays are derived from saved bob mass, world.g and world.n. The spring and rods are massless; the displayed bob spheres are not extra inertia.
Geometry includes a fixed support beam and floor as unconnected visual references; contact and spring-coil collision are not simulated.

notes: Problem 68, Mechanics I, Newton's Laws: lighter bob rises 1.4 m in two seconds. Absolute masses 13 kg and 15 kg and display geometry are illustrative choices.
Oppositely oriented MSL MultiBody Prismatic joints are coupled through one massless MSL Translational Rod(L=0) kinematic constraint. This enforces a taut ideal rope without prescribing a trajectory.
The pulley is a fixed visual object: there is no modeled wheel rotation or inertia. The rope's straight sections are native time-varying MSL shapes.
Tension overlays use native joint translational-port flow forces. Weight vectors are derived from saved native mass and uniform gravity parameters.
This bilateral constraint excludes slack, recontact, friction, contact, impact and pulley rotational dynamics.
